The four stored templates, application stylesheet and upstream images retain
their original bytes. source.json records SHA-256 and Git blob SHA-1 values.
Bootstrap 4.3.1 is served locally; its SHA-384 equals the integrity attribute
already present in the official layout. No custom storefront CSS is loaded.

Runtime adaptation is isolated in lib/storefront/native-render.mjs and
public/store/app.js. The renderer performs the original template substitutions,
mounts links and assets under /store/, and replaces the external Adyen SDK and
Adyen implementation script with the local controller bridge. It does not
translate or rewrite the original Cart or result text, layout, or styles.

The official preview is intentionally a fixed cart containing one Sunglasses
and one Headphones, each 50.00, total 100.00. The bridge prepares exactly those
backend quantities and verifies the total before checkout. Local ledger units
remain TEST_USDC; the fixed original UI does not display a currency symbol.
The mechanism page identifies this as a local simulation.

The upstream payment slot is empty without an Adyen client key and session.
After actual credential/holder/device verification succeeds, the bridge adds
one button, 'Pay 100.00', using the existing upstream .button class. Clicking it
explicitly approves the matching Owner proposal, then invokes the original
local x402 payment controller. This button is the necessary local payment
adapter, not an Adyen component, card form or external payment integration.
No merchant account, Adyen SDK or real payment service is connected.

The success/pending/failed result copy and artwork are rendered from the
official result template. Server-side controller state decides which result
can be shown; a URL alone does not assert a successful payment. Detailed
authorization, simulation and merchant-recovery evidence belongs to the
separate mechanism page.

Provenance check: node scripts/native-mystore-source-check.mjs
